standard.title: Citation and Reference for Publicly Available Information, Commercially Available Information, and Open Source Intelligence
standard.summary: Extends ICD 206 with citation conventions specific to Publicly Available Information (PAI), Commercially Available Information (CAI), Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), and AI-generated content. Governs how these source types appear in disseminated and covered analytic products.

src-conventions.rule: Separate SRC metadata fields with a pipe character (`|`).
Place the source descriptor in the last piped section. Use commas to separate concepts within the descriptor.

Default to descriptive SRCs that support discovery and reproducibility. Generic SRCs are the exception, used only when there are evidence-based security concerns (e.g. risk of behaviour change or diminished source access).

element.description: The internal IC entity that created or wrote the analysis --- which may be distinct from the entity that collected the data.
element.convention: Use the "OSINT Analysis by [element]" tagline when the content represents the element's coordinated analytic position ("we assess", "OSINT reveals", thesis-driven argumentation) --- not for data gathering, translation, repackaging, or curation alone.

element.description: External author of the source content, distinct from internal IC authorship. If the author is a US Person, follow applicable masking rules and IC element guidelines.
URL of the source, collection tool used, third-party data or analytics service provider, or a placeholder number (coordinated with the IC OSINT Executive) when sensitivity prevents direct citation.

source-descriptor-elements.element:
Brief description of the source's credibility, biases, and quality of information.
PlatformXYZ, hosted by think tank Y, has a mission statement to increase public spending on X. Guest authors produce fact-based, original research but often from Y's policy position.

element.description: The entity that researched, gathered, or collected the data.
Name of the database, relevant technical or content information, and whether a login was required.
element.example: Article retrieved from Database_Company commercial database, specialises in climate change content, login required.

element.description: Name the tool or data service used. Must be cited if it provided judgment calls, recommendations, inferences, or predictions ("value added analytics") --- especially when AI/ML/CV-assisted. Traditional programming functions (search, summation, keyword alerting, spreadsheet-like functions) do not require notation.

ai-citation.rule: Cite any AI system used for collection or analysis whenever it contributes judgment, inference, or value-added analytics to the product.

citation-type.description: For AI systems that classify or detect (e.g. computer vision finding construction equipment in imagery).

required-elements.element: brief non-technical explanation of what the system does
GitHub or software code link (if open source)

citation-type.example: Computer Vision System, Look At Those Cars (LATC), finds construction equipment in commercial electro-optical imagery, Model Precision 90% --- Recall 75%, trained on 2,000 labelled commercial electro-optical images from March 2019 to April 2024, Version 2.1, www.github.com/latc, system used for project to identify cranes 1--5 July 2024.

citation-type.description: For generative AI outputs (stochastic --- the same prompt may produce different outputs). Documenting the base elements is essential for reproducibility.
citation-type.caveat: Outputs are stochastic. The same prompt may produce different outputs on different runs.
citation-type.example: TalkXYZ platform or model used, prompt: "Generate a report on the city of Beijing. Tell me about the history of the city. Write this in a formal tone. Include citations from National Geographic."

retention.rule: If an externally-created PAI or CAI source is dynamic and important to the bottom-line message, preserve a record (e.g. screen print) for at least one year. Follow the IC element's NARA-approved Records Control Schedule; the RCS prevails in conflict.
For long-horizon products (e.g. National Intelligence Estimates), retain PAI or CAI source citations for the product's time horizon or five years, whichever is shorter.

glossary.definition: A machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments (per 15 U.S.C. § 9401(3)).
Data or information customarily sold, leased, or licensed to the general public or to non-governmental entities --- including data provided voluntarily to the government by corporate entities.
Information that has been published or broadcast for public consumption, is available on request to the public, is accessible online, or could be seen or heard by any casual observer.
Intelligence derived exclusively from publicly or commercially available information that addresses specific intelligence priorities, requirements, or gaps.
An analytic product representing an IC element's coordinated analytic position, derived solely from PAI, CAI, and/or OSINT and disseminated broadly.
An OSINT product that provides "fact of" observations and informational content without analysis or a coordinated analytic position.
The practice of hyperlinking words and phrases to the underlying online source. Does not negate the need for source metadata; direct links and endnotes can co-exist.

definition.term: Source Validation of PAI and CAI

glossary.definition: The process of identifying a PAI or CAI source's reporting significance --- focused on determining accuracy and reliability.
PAI or CAI that has been collected but not yet determined to meet the criteria for IC-element retention.
